Overview

The Hunza Valley 9-Day Tour is a mesmerizing journey through Pakistan’s most picturesque landscapes. From the ancient forts of Hunza to the breathtaking views of Khunjerab Pass, this trip is designed for travelers seeking a perfect blend of adventure, history, and cultural exploration. The expedition covers Islamabad, Gilgit, Hunza, Attabad Lake, Gojal Valley, and Naltar Valley, offering a well-rounded experience of northern Pakistan.

Why This Tour?

  • Unparalleled Beauty: Experience the stunning landscapes of Rakaposhi Viewpoint, Passu Cones, and Khunjerab National Park.
  • Rich Heritage: Visit ancient Baltit Fort, Altit Fort, and the Royal Garden for a deep dive into Hunza’s history.
  • Cultural Immersion: Engage with local communities, enjoy traditional Hunza cuisine, and explore vibrant bazaars.
  • Adventure & Serenity: Enjoy serene lakes, scenic hikes, and breathtaking mountain views all in one trip.

Itinerary

Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad

Upon arrival at Islamabad International Airport, you will be greeted by our team and transferred to your hotel. After checking in, take the rest of the day to unwind from your flight. In the evening, meet your fellow travelers over a welcome dinner, and if time allows, explore the city’s local shops and markets.

Stay Options
Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 2: Flight to Gilgit – Journey into Hunza

Begin the day with a scenic flight to Gilgit, where you will catch aerial glimpses of snow-capped peaks, weather permitting. From Gilgit, drive through stunning mountain roads into Hunza Valley, pausing at the Rakaposhi View Point for breathtaking photo opportunities. Upon arrival, immerse yourself in Hunza’s rich heritage by visiting the ancient Baltit Fort, wandering through Karimabad Bazaar, and admiring the historic Altit Fort. End the day in Duikar, the highest vantage point in Central Hunza, to witness a captivating sunset before settling into your hotel.

Stay Options
Premium: Hunza Serena Hotel
Luxury: Eagles Nest Hotel
Standard: Ayash Resort

Day 3: Attabad Lake and Gulmit Village

Today, travel through the impressive Attabad Tunnels to reach the renowned Attabad Lake. Marvel at its turquoise waters, which offer a striking contrast against the towering mountains. Later, head into Gojal Valley and check in at a lakeside resort. Spend the afternoon exploring Gulmit Village, a region known for its warm hospitality and scenic surroundings. If you are feeling adventurous, hike up the Ondra Poyga trail to Kamaris Village for sweeping panoramic views before returning for a restful evening.

Stay Options
Premium: Luxus Resort Hunza
Luxury: Famree Resort
Standard: Silk Route Lodge

Day 4: Khunjerab National Park – Pak-China Border

Depart early for Khunjerab National Park, driving past the historic Hussaini Suspension Bridge and the majestic Passu Cones, also known as Cathedral Peaks. As you enter the park, keep an eye out for wildlife such as ibex or even the elusive snow leopard. Continue onward to the Pak-China Border at Khunjerab Pass, one of the highest paved international border crossings in the world. After soaking in the high-altitude scenery, return to your hotel near Attabad Lake for a tranquil night’s rest.

Stay Options
Premium: Luxus Resort Hunza
Luxury: Famree Resort
Standard: Silk Route Lodge

Day 5: Nagar Valley and Hoper Glacier

Embark on a journey to Nagar Valley, a region celebrated for its lush landscapes and imposing glaciers. Make your way to the Hope Glacier View Point, where a short hike leads you to mesmerizing ice formations. Enjoy some free time to wander around and capture photos of the soaring peaks and verdant hills. As evening falls, drive back to Hunza to spend a relaxed evening at your hotel.

Stay Options
Premium: Hunza Serena Inn
Luxury: Eagles Nest Hotel
Standard: Ayash Resort

Day 6: Naltar Valley – Satrangi Lake

Venture through the mountain village of Nomal to reach Naltar Valley, famous for its pristine forests and serene alpine lakes. Explore the Naltar Wildlife Sanctuary, where you can admire local flora and fauna. A highlight of this region is Satrangi Lake, known for its vivid, multicolored reflections that change with the light. Conclude the day with a drive to Gilgit, where you will check in at your hotel and, if time permits, visit Kargah Buddha and the NLI Market.

Stay Options
Premium: Gilgit Serena Hotel
Luxury: Riverdale Hotel
Standard: Mandarin Inn

Day 7: Return to Islamabad – Leisure Day

After breakfast, head to the airport in Gilgit for a short flight back to Islamabad. Upon arrival, transfer to your hotel, where you can relax or use the remaining time to discover the capital city’s modern comforts and cultural gems. Sample local cuisine, visit nearby shops, or simply unwind at the hotel after your days of exploration in the north.

Stay Options
Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 8: Islamabad City Tour

Spend the day touring the capital, beginning with the iconic Faisal Mosque, renowned for its contemporary architecture. Proceed to the Islamabad Monument and Pakistan Museum to learn about the nation’s history and cultural achievements. Afterward, head to Daman-e-Koh for sweeping views of the city below. You will have free time in the evening for last-minute shopping or savoring the city’s diverse culinary scene.

Stay Options
Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 9: Departure

Conclude your journey by transferring to the airport for your flight home. Carry memories of the enchanting Hunza landscapes, cultural insights, and new friendships made along the way.

Packing List

Spring Packing Checklist for Northern Pakistan - Summit Experts

Spring (late-March to May) is one of the best seasons to explore Northern Pakistan, with mild weather, blooming flowers, and lush green landscapes. To make sure you have a comfortable and enjoyable journey, we’ve prepared a comprehensive packing list for your adventure.

Essential Packing Categories:

  1. Luggage & Bags
    • Main Luggage (70-80L): A sturdy, spacious bag for all your essentials. Ensure it has waterproof covers for unexpected weather.
    • Daypack (30-40L): Ideal for carrying daily items like snacks, water, and your camera during excursions.
    • Padlocks: Secure your belongings during travel.
  2. Clothing
    • Upper Body:
      • Lightweight Jacket: Perfect for chilly mornings and evenings. Consider a windbreaker or fleece.
      • Long-Sleeve Shirts & T-Shirts: Comfortable, breathable fabrics are ideal for layering.
      • Rain Jacket: Waterproof and wind-resistant for unexpected spring showers.
    • Lower Body:
      • Trekking Trousers: Lightweight and quick-drying trousers for hikes and outdoor activities.
      • Comfortable Pants/Jeans: Suitable for both city tours and countryside visits.
    • General Tips:
      • Layer Up: The weather can vary, so layers will help you adjust to temperature changes.
      • Respect Local Culture: Modest clothing is recommended, especially in towns and cultural sites.
  3. Footwear
    • Hiking Boots: Well-worn, waterproof boots with good ankle support for trekking.
    • Comfortable Walking Shoes: For city exploration and casual outings.
    • Warm Socks: Preferably made of moisture-wicking material.
  4. Accessories
    • Sunblock (SPF 50+): Protects against strong UV rays.
    • Hat/Cap: For sun protection during hikes and outdoor tours.
    • Sunglasses: Good UV protection for your eyes.
    • Light Scarf/Bandana: Useful for dust protection and sun cover.
  5. Toiletries & Personal Care
    • Compact Toiletry Kit: Include essentials like toothpaste, deodorant, and moisturizer.
    • Travel Towel: Quick-drying and lightweight.
    • Wet Wipes & Hand Sanitizer: For maintaining hygiene during day trips.
  6. Hydration & Snacks
    • Reusable Water Bottle (Insulated Preferred): Stay hydrated, especially during hikes.
    • Energy Bars & Snacks: Lightweight snacks for quick energy boosts.
  7. Tech & Gadgets
    • Camera & Accessories: Capture stunning landscapes and cultural moments. Bring extra memory cards.
    • Power Bank: Essential for keeping devices charged on the go.
    • Travel Adapter: Ensure compatibility with local sockets.
  8. Important Documents
    • Passport: Must have at least six months of validity remaining.
    • Visa & Travel Insurance: Check visa requirements and carry printouts of your insurance details.
    • Emergency Contact Information: A printed list of important contacts.

Tips for Spring Travel

  • Prepare for Variable Weather: Spring can bring unexpected showers, so a waterproof jacket and protective covers for your belongings are recommended.
  • Comfortable Layers: Temperatures fluctuate, so plan for both warm afternoons and cool evenings.
  • Be Ready for Long Walks: Comfortable shoes and a light backpack will make your excursions more enjoyable.

Why Travel with Summit Experts?

Our experienced team ensures that your journey is not just comfortable, but also safe and unforgettable. We provide personalized packing recommendations based on your specific tour itinerary, and our guides are always ready to help you with any last-minute needs.

A Journey to Remember
I just returned from an incredible month-long adventure in northern Pakistan with Summit Experts Adventure Tours. We trekked through some of the most breathtaking regions: Skardu, Hunza, Shimshal Village, and made our way to Shimshal Pass, ending with the exhilarating summit of Manglik Sar (6050m). Overview

About This Trip

Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan, is a city that blends modernity with nature and history. This full-day tour offers an immersive experience of Islamabad’s rich culture, breathtaking landscapes, and historical landmarks. From the grandeur of Faisal Mosque to the cultural insights at Lok Virsa Museum, and the panoramic views from Daman-e-Koh, this trip provides the perfect balance of sightseeing and relaxation. Whether you are a history enthusiast, nature lover, or simply want to explore Pakistan’s capital, this tour is designed to give you an unforgettable experience.

Why This Tour?

✅ Comprehensive Exploration – Visit Islamabad’s most famous landmarks in just one day.
✅ Cultural Immersion – Explore Lok Virsa Museum and Pakistan Monument Museum to learn about the country’s rich history and heritage.
✅ Scenic Beauty – Experience breathtaking views of the city from Daman-e-Koh and the Margalla Hills.
✅ Optional Adventure – Enjoy a short hike on Trail 3 or 5 for a stunning sunset experience.
✅ Hassle-Free Experience – A guided tour with hotel pick-up and drop-off ensures a comfortable and well-organized trip.

Itinerary

Your guide will pick you up from your hotel, and we’ll start our day exploring the capital city of Pakistan.

Faisal Mosque

Visit Faisal Mosque, an iconic landmark and the largest mosque in Pakistan, set against the stunning backdrop of the Margalla Hills.

Pakistan Monument & Museum

Explore the Pakistan Monument, a national symbol representing unity, and visit the Pakistan Monument Museum to learn about Pakistan’s history.

Lok Virsa Museum

A cultural museum showcasing the diverse traditions, arts, and crafts from different regions of Pakistan.

Daman-e-Koh Viewpoint

Enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of Islamabad from Daman-e-Koh, a scenic spot in the Margalla Hills.

Lunch at a Local Restaurant

We will stop for lunch at a top-rated restaurant in Islamabad.

Sunset at Margalla Hills (Optional Short Hike – Trail 3 or 5)

For those who love adventure, we can take a short scenic hike on Trail 3 or Trail 5 and enjoy the stunning sunset views over Islamabad.

Drop-off at Hotel

  • End of the tour! Your guide will drop you back at your hotel after an exciting day in Islamabad.

    (Tour Starts and Ends in Islamabad – If some other city additional Charges will apply)

Key Information

  • Destinations Covered: Faisal Mosque, Pakistan Monument, Lok Virsa Museum, Daman-e-Koh, Margalla Hills Trail 3 or 5 (optional hike).
  • Tour Duration: Full-day tour (6-8 hours).
  • Best Season: Year-round (Spring & Autumn offer the best weather).
  • Difficulty Level: Easy – Suitable for all ages, with minimal walking (hike is optional).
  • Starting & Ending Point: Islamabad (Hotel pickup & drop-off included).

  • Meals: Lunch

  • Additional Costs: Entry fees (if applicable), personal expenses, and optional hiking gear.
  • Customizations: Available upon request (special pickup from another city may incur additional charges).

Overview

About Expedition

The K2 Base Camp Trek is one of the most iconic and challenging trekking adventures in the world. Taking you deep into the heart of the Karakoram, this 21-day expedition offers breathtaking views of towering peaks, including K2 (8,611m), Broad Peak, and the Trango Towers. The journey follows the legendary Baltoro Glacier, leading to Concordia, the “Throne Room of the Mountain Gods,” where some of the world’s highest peaks surround you. Ideal for seasoned trekkers, this trek offers a rare opportunity to witness the grandeur of Pakistan’s remote wilderness.

Why This Trek?

  • Unparalleled Scenery: Experience breathtaking views of K2, Broad Peak, and Gasherbrum peaks.
  • Challenging and Rewarding: Trek through one of the world’s most rugged and remote landscapes.
  • Cultural Exploration: Visit Skardu and the remote village of Askole, the last human settlement before the Karakoram wilderness.
  • Ultimate Adventure: Ideal for experienced trekkers looking for a high-altitude expedition.

Itinerary

Day 01: Arrival at Islamabad International Airport

Altitude: 540 m
Upon your arrival at Islamabad International Airport, you will receive a warm welcome from our friendly guide(s). They will assist you with your transfer to the hotel, where you can unwind and recover from your journey.

Pickup Information:
Our guides will be easily recognizable, holding placards adorned with our company logo and your name. Please make sure to arrive at Islamabad International Airport, as most international flights arrive late at night or in the afternoon. We kindly request that you provide us with your flight details—both inbound and outbound—at least five days prior to your arrival. Our staff will greet you at the international arrivals gate unless you are connecting from another city in Pakistan. If you do not require an airport transfer, please inform us in advance.

After enjoying lunch and some rest at the hotel (ideally for those arriving in the morning between 9 AM and 12 PM), our representative will gather all guests at 6 PM for a briefing and to settle any outstanding payments at our office, followed by a delightful dinner. If your arrival is later in the day, we will arrange for payments and the briefing in Skardu.

Day 02: Flight to Skardu, Karakoram

Altitude: 2,498 m
Participants will embark on a stunning morning flight from Islamabad to Skardu Airport, weather permitting, with breathtaking views of Nanga Parbat. Upon arrival in Skardu, the remainder of the day is yours to explore at your leisure.

Day 03: Free Day in Skardu

Altitude: 2,498 m
After a hearty breakfast, you may choose to hike to Kharpocho Fort, perched atop a mountain and offering magnificent views of the Indus River and Skardu town. An optional tour to the picturesque Sadpara Lake will be available, followed by free time for shopping in the bustling Skardu Bazaar.

Throughout the day, our dedicated staff will manage any necessary government documentation, which may take up to two days. We have incorporated contingency days at the end of the trek to accommodate any potential delays.

Day 04: Drive to Askole Village

Altitude: 3,015 m
Your adventure begins with a jeep safari towards Daso, traversing the enchanting Shigar Valley. This journey follows the banks of the Braldu River, leading you to Askole—the last village on our route. Depending on road conditions, you may begin your trek before reaching Askole. The journey will take approximately 6 to 8 hours.

Day 05: Trek from Askole to Jhola via Biafo Glacier Snout

Altitude: 3,103 m
Distance: 20 km
Duration: 5-8 hours
After finalizing the necessary supplies and equipment, porters will load up for the trek to Jhola. Experience the thrill of moraine walking as you cross the glacier’s snout and descend to a scenic lunch spot by the Korofon River. The trail leads to the confluence of the Braldu and Domordo Rivers, where you will traverse a newer trail upstream, crossing a bridge before descending to the camp at Jhola.

Day 06: Trek from Jhola to Paiju along Braldu River

Altitude: 3,418 m
Distance: 19.8 km
Duration: 6-7 hours
Follow the Braldu gorge alongside the river, with captivating views of the magnificent Trango Towers and Cathedral Peak. Given the potentially dry and hot conditions, sun protection is advised. Depending on water levels, river crossing shoes may be necessary. On a clear day, the snout of Baltoro Glacier will be visible. Your day concludes with a climb away from the river to camp at Paiju, the last campsite with trees for a while.

Day 07: Acclimatization and Rest at Paiju

Altitude: 3,418 m
Spend the day at Paiju Camp for essential acclimatization and relaxation. Meanwhile, our porters will prepare fresh bread for the upcoming days on the glacier. An acclimatization walk to the base of Paiju Peak is also available for those who wish to explore.

Day 08: Trek from Paiju to Khoburtse

Altitude: 3,788 m
Distance: 14.7 km
Duration: 5-7 hours
As you trek towards the snout of Baltoro Glacier, the journey becomes more challenging, but the scenery becomes increasingly spectacular. The trail involves continuous ascents and descents over glacial moraine, so please exercise caution. You will be rewarded with stunning views of Trango Tower and Uli Biaho. The day concludes with a traverse of the glacier to Liligo, before arriving at camp at Khoburtse.

Day 09: Cross Small Glaciers and Walk to Urdukus

Altitude: 3,905 m
Distance: 6.4 km
Duration: 4-6 hours
After navigating two small glaciers, you will arrive at Urdukas, conveniently located near an army camp and 100 meters above the glacier.

Day 10: Trek to Goro II, Junction of Baltoro and Younghusband Glaciers

Altitude: 4,285 m
Distance: 11.9 km
Duration: 6-8 hours
Your trek continues through the heart of the glacier, following the medial moraine while enjoying views of the majestic Masherbrum (7,821 m). This trek involves climbing over rocky moraine and passing colossal ice seracs. Goro II, our first camp on Baltoro Glacier, marks the confluence of Baltoro and Younghusband Glaciers. Prepare for significantly cooler temperatures and breathtaking vistas of Masherbrum and Muztagh Tower.

Day 11: Trek to Concordia via Rocky Moraine

Altitude: 4,512 m
Distance: 11.7 km
Duration: 5-7 hours
As you ascend the moraine to reach Concordia, you will be rewarded with awe-inspiring views of K2, Broad Peak, Mitre Peak, Gasherbrum, Sia Kangri, and more.

Day 12: Trek to Broad Peak Base Camp, Gilkey Memorial, and K2 Base Camp

Altitude: K2 Base Camp (5,155 m), Gilkey (5,230 m), Broad Peak (4,844 m)
Duration: 6-7 hours
This remarkable trek allows you to walk up the Godwin-Austen glacier to the Art Gilkey Memorial, commemorating those lost on K2. Departing early, you will cross glaciers along a faint trail towards K2, which will loom ever larger. After a lunch stop at Broad Peak Base Camp, the group will continue toward K2 Base Camp, where the landscape is adorned with boulders and ice. Overnight will be spent at K2 Base Camp. Should you feel unwell on this day and prefer not to stay at K2 Base Camp, we encourage you to consult your guide, as we prioritize the dreams and well-being of all trekkers.

Day 13: Return Trek to Concordia

Duration: 4-5 hours
Participants will retrace their steps back to Concordia, where you can rest and prepare for the next day’s journey.

Day 14: Trek to Goro I/Biango

Altitude: 4,010 m
Distance: 15.9 km
Duration: 6-7 hours
You will leave camp and make your way back to Goro I, enjoying a more leisurely trek as you descend.

Day 15: Trek to Khoburtse with Views of Trango Towers

Altitude: 3,788 m
Distance: 13.8 km
Duration: 5-7 hours
As you descend towards the campsite at Urdukas, you will follow the same trail but enjoy fresh perspectives on the stunning Trango Towers.

Day 16: Return Trek to Camp Paiju

Altitude: 3,418 m
Distance: 14.7 km
Duration: 5-7 hours
Your trek will take you down the glacier’s side via Liligo, transitioning to more stable terrain. Upon your arrival at Paiju Camp, you will be greeted by the refreshing sight of trees.

Day 17: Trek to Jhola Campsite

Altitude: 3,418 m
Distance: 19.8 km
Duration: 5-7 hours
You will follow the same route back through Braldu Gorge, with potential river crossings, concluding your day at Jhola.

Day 18: Trek to Askole and Drive to Skardu Town

Altitude: 2,498 m
Distance: 20 km trek + 127 km drive
Duration: 5-7 hours trek + 6 hours drive
You will trek back to Askole village and then transfer to Skardu by jeep after lunch, providing a well-deserved rest for your feet.

Day 19: Flight to Islamabad

On this day, you will fly from Skardu Airport to Islamabad Airport, providing an opportunity to relax at the hotel upon your arrival. Please note that domestic flights may be subject to cancellation due to weather conditions. In the event of a cancellation, participants will be transported to Naran/Besham for an overnight

Day 20: Contingency Day for Flight Cancellation

This day has been thoughtfully reserved for any potential delays should the domestic flight not operate as scheduled. If necessary, guests will depart early from Chilas to Islamabad, which may take up to ten hours. However, if participants successfully reach Islamabad via the domestic flight, this day will be free for delightful sightseeing and exploration of the vibrant city.

Day 21: Departure to Home Country

Meals Included: Breakfast
On your final day, our attentive staff will assist all guests with their transfers to the airport in accordance with your respective departure times. Please remember that the checkout time for all partner hotels is set at 12 PM. We wish you safe travels and fond memories as you return home!

Day 06: Trek from Jhola to Paiju along Braldu River

Altitude: 3,418 m
Distance: 19.8 km
Duration: 6-7 hours
Follow the Braldu gorge alongside the river, with captivating views of the magnificent Trango Towers and Cathedral Peak. Given the potentially dry and hot conditions, sun protection is advised. Depending on water levels, river crossing shoes may be necessary. On a clear day, the snout of Baltoro Glacier will be visible. Your day concludes with a climb away from the river to camp at Paiju, the last campsite with trees for a while.

Day 07: Acclimatization and Rest at Paiju

Altitude: 3,418 m
Spend the day at Paiju Camp for essential acclimatization and relaxation. Meanwhile, our porters will prepare fresh bread for the upcoming days on the glacier. An acclimatization walk to the base of Paiju Peak is also available for those who wish to explore.

Day 08: Trek from Paiju to Khoburtse

Altitude: 3,788 m
Distance: 14.7 km
Duration: 5-7 hours
As you trek towards the snout of Baltoro Glacier, the journey becomes more challenging, but the scenery becomes increasingly spectacular. The trail involves continuous ascents and descents over glacial moraine, so please exercise caution. You will be rewarded with stunning views of Trango Tower and Uli Biaho. The day concludes with a traverse of the glacier to Liligo, before arriving at camp at Khoburtse.

Day 09: Cross Small Glaciers and Walk to Urdukus

Altitude: 3,905 m
Distance: 6.4 km
Duration: 4-6 hours
After navigating two small glaciers, you will arrive at Urdukas, conveniently located near an army camp and 100 meters above the glacier.

Day 10: Trek to Goro II, Junction of Baltoro and Younghusband Glaciers

Altitude: 4,285 m
Distance: 11.9 km
Duration: 6-8 hours
Your trek continues through the heart of the glacier, following the medial moraine while enjoying views of the majestic Masherbrum (7,821 m). This trek involves climbing over rocky moraine and passing colossal ice seracs. Goro II, our first camp on Baltoro Glacier, marks the confluence of Baltoro and Younghusband Glaciers. Prepare for significantly cooler temperatures and breathtaking vistas of Masherbrum and Muztagh Tower.

Day 11: Trek to Concordia via Rocky Moraine

Altitude: 4,512 m
Distance: 11.7 km
Duration: 5-7 hours
As you ascend the moraine to reach Concordia, you will be rewarded with awe-inspiring views of K2, Broad Peak, Mitre Peak, Gasherbrum, Sia Kangri, and more.

Day 12: Trek to Broad Peak Base Camp, Gilkey Memorial, and K2 Base Camp

Altitude: K2 Base Camp (5,155 m), Gilkey (5,230 m), Broad Peak (4,844 m)
Duration: 6-7 hours
This remarkable trek allows you to walk up the Godwin-Austen glacier to the Art Gilkey Memorial, commemorating those lost on K2. Departing early, you will cross glaciers along a faint trail towards K2, which will loom ever larger. After a lunch stop at Broad Peak Base Camp, the group will continue toward K2 Base Camp, where the landscape is adorned with boulders and ice. Overnight will be spent at K2 Base Camp. Should you feel unwell on this day and prefer not to stay at K2 Base Camp, we encourage you to consult your guide, as we prioritize the dreams and well-being of all trekkers.

Day 13: Return Trek to Concordia

Duration: 4-5 hours
Participants will retrace their steps back to Concordia, where you can rest and prepare for the next day’s journey.

Day 14: Trek to Goro I/Biango

Altitude: 4,010 m
Distance: 15.9 km
Duration: 6-7 hours
You will leave camp and make your way back to Goro I, enjoying a more leisurely trek as you descend.

Day 15: Trek to Khoburtse with Views of Trango Towers

Altitude: 3,788 m
Distance: 13.8 km
Duration: 5-7 hours
As you descend towards the campsite at Urdukas, you will follow the same trail but enjoy fresh perspectives on the stunning Trango Towers.

Day 16: Return Trek to Camp Paiju

Altitude: 3,418 m
Distance: 14.7 km
Duration: 5-7 hours
Your trek will take you down the glacier’s side via Liligo, transitioning to more stable terrain. Upon your arrival at Paiju Camp, you will be greeted by the refreshing sight of trees.

Day 17: Trek to Jhola Campsite

Altitude: 3,418 m
Distance: 19.8 km
Duration: 5-7 hours
You will follow the same route back through Braldu Gorge, with potential river crossings, concluding your day at Jhola.

Day 18: Trek to Askole and Drive to Skardu Town

Altitude: 2,498 m
Distance: 20 km trek + 127 km drive
Duration: 5-7 hours trek + 6 hours drive
You will trek back to Askole village and then transfer to Skardu by jeep after lunch, providing a well-deserved rest for your feet.

Day 19: Flight to Islamabad

On this day, you will fly from Skardu Airport to Islamabad Airport, providing an opportunity to relax at the hotel upon your arrival. Please note that domestic flights may be subject to cancellation due to weather conditions. In the event of a cancellation, participants will be transported to Naran/Besham for an overnight

Day 20: Contingency Day for Flight Cancellation

This day has been thoughtfully reserved for any potential delays should the domestic flight not operate as scheduled. If necessary, guests will depart early from Chilas to Islamabad, which may take up to ten hours. However, if participants successfully reach Islamabad via the domestic flight, this day will be free for delightful sightseeing and exploration of the vibrant city.

Day 21: Departure to Home Country

Meals Included: Breakfast
On your final day, our attentive staff will assist all guests with their transfers to the airport in accordance with your respective departure times. Please remember that the checkout time for all partner hotels is set at 12 PM. We wish you safe travels and fond memories as you return home!

Packing List

Preparing for the K2 Base Camp Trek requires the right equipment to ensure safety, comfort, and success. Whether navigating the rugged terrains of the Baltoro Glacier or enduring high-altitude weather conditions, proper gear is crucial. Below is a carefully curated packing guide to help you trek confidently through one of the world’s most iconic routes.

Essential Equipment (Must-Have Items)

  • Backpack & Storage:
    • Large duffel bag for main gear (carried by porters)
    • 32–42 liter daypack for personal items
    • Waterproof pack cover
  • Clothing:
    • Insulating layers (fleece jacket, thermal base layers)
    • Down jacket (-16°C rating recommended)
    • Waterproof and windproof outerwear (jacket and trousers)
    • Trekking trousers and shorts
    • High-quality trekking socks (multiple pairs)
    • Lightweight gloves and insulated gloves
    • Sun hat, beanie, and buff/scarf
  • Footwear:
    • Sturdy, well-worn trekking boots (waterproof)
    • Camp shoes or sandals for resting
    • Gaiters (optional for snow conditions)
  • Sleeping & Camping Gear:
    • Sleeping bag (-16°C to -20°C comfort rating)
    • Inflatable or foam sleeping mat
    • Sleeping bag liner (optional for extra warmth)
  • Trekking Accessories:
    • Trekking poles (strongly recommended for stability)
    • UV-protection sunglasses
    • Head torch with extra batteries
    • Reusable water bottles (minimum 2 liters)
    • Water purification tablets or a filtration system

Recommended Gear (For Extra Comfort & Convenience)

  • Personal Hygiene & Health:
    • Antibacterial hand gel & wet wipes
    • Toothbrush, toothpaste & biodegradable soap
    • Quick-dry travel towel
    • Lip balm & high-SPF sunscreen
    • Blister patches & personal first-aid kit
    • Personal medication (Diamox for altitude sickness if prescribed)
  • Electronics & Miscellaneous:
    • Power bank or solar charger (as electrical generators may not be allowed in the Baltoro region)
    • Camera with extra batteries & memory cards
    • Notebook & pen (for journaling)
    • Snacks (energy bars, trail mix, chocolate, etc.)
    • Small padlock for securing trek bag

Important Notice

Due to government regulations, electrical generators may be restricted in the Baltoro region. While we provide solar-powered lighting and satellite communication, we highly recommend bringing a solar charger or high-capacity power bank to keep your personal devices powered throughout the trek.

Ensure you’re well-prepared to embrace the breathtaking landscapes of the Karakoram Range and conquer the K2 Base Camp with confidence! For any further inquiries, feel free to contact our team for personalized gear recommendations.

FAQs

01

What are the best months for trekking in Pakistan?

+

 The best trekking season is from June to September, when temperatures are stable, and most passes are snow-free. For treks involving Gondogoro La Pass, July and August offer and for Snow Lake August is the safest conditions.

02

How physically demanding are these treks?

+

Each trek varies in difficulty:

  • K2 Base Camp Trek – Strenuous but non-technical, requiring good fitness.
  • Snow Lake Trek – Challenging due to glacier travel and isolation.
  • K2 Base Camp & Gondogoro La Circuit Trek – Demanding, with technical sections requiring crampons.
03

Do I need prior trekking experience?

+

Experience is not mandatory but recommended. You should be comfortable walking 6-8 hours per day on rocky and glacial terrain. Proper physical preparation is essential.

04

What permits do I need?

+
  • K2 Base Camp & Gondogoro La Trek require a special Mountaineering & Trekking Visa (not a regular tourist visa).
  • Snow Lake Trek requires a regular visa as this is not located in a restricted zone, which we arrange for you.
05

What happens in case of an emergency?

+
  • Our guides carry satellite phones for emergencies.
  • If altitude sickness occurs, you will be escorted to a lower altitude.
  • In severe cases, a helicopter rescue can be arranged (insurance required).
06

What fitness level and skills are required for K2 Treks?

+
  • K2 Base Camp Trek: Suitable for fit individuals with previous hiking experience. Trekkers walk 6-8 miles per day for 5-6 hours on rough terrain.

Gondogoro La Pass: Requires use of crampons and ropes due to snow, ice, and steeper climbs.

07

How far will we walk each day?

+
  • K2 Base Camp Trek: Expect to walk 8 to 14 km per day, taking 6-8 hours.
  • Gondogoro La Pass: The crossing day can take 8-12 hours, depending on snow conditions.
08

What’s the most challenging section of the trek?

+
  • K2 Base Camp Trek: The trek from Concordia to K2 Base Camp is challenging due to altitude and glacier terrain.
  • Gondogoro La Pass: The most difficult part is the steep ascent and descent over icy slopes.
09

How long is the K2 Base Camp Trek?

+

 The standard itinerary is 20 days, including acclimatization and travel days.

10

What is the highest altitude reached?

+

K2 Base Camp sits at 5,125m.

11

Are there rest days?

+

 Yes, acclimatization days are included to prevent altitude sickness.

12

Is mobile network available on this trek?

+

Only in Skardu and Askole. Limited connectivity is available in Concordia (7 AM - 7 PM).

13

What happens if the weather prevents a summit attempt?

+

 If the weather prevents progress, we may wait or modify the itinerary. Safety always comes first.

Overview

About Expedition

The K2 Gondogoro La Circuit Trek is an extension of the classic K2 Base Camp trek, taking adventure seekers beyond Concordia to cross the spectacular Gondogoro La Pass (5,585m). This trek provides an unparalleled view of the Karakoram’s highest peaks while adding an element of technical climbing to the experience. The circuit trek allows trekkers to complete a loop rather than retracing their steps, offering a unique perspective on this high-altitude wonderland.

Why This Trek?

  • 360° Panoramic Views: Witness K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum I & II, and the mesmerizing valleys from Gondogoro La Pass.
  • More Challenging, More Rewarding: This trek is for those who want to push their limits and experience true mountaineering.
  • Remote & Less Traveled: Unlike the standard K2 Base Camp Trek, this circuit takes you off the beaten path.
  • A True Alpine Experience: Experience both glacier trekking and high-altitude pass crossing in one trip.

Itinerary

Day 01: Arrival at Islamabad International Airport

Overview
• Altitude: 540 m
Upon your arrival at Islamabad International Airport, our friendly guide will be there to greet you and assist with your transfer to the hotel. This day is dedicated to relaxation and recovery from your journey.

Pickup Information
Our guide will be easily identifiable, holding a placard featuring our company’s logo along with your name. To ensure a smooth experience, please provide your international flight details—both inbound and outbound—at least five days before your arrival in Pakistan. Our guide will meet you at the international arrivals gate unless you are connecting from another city in Pakistan. If you do not require an airport transfer, kindly inform us in advance.

After enjoying lunch and a brief rest (ideal for arrivals between 9 AM and 12 PM), our guide will gather all guests around 6 PM for a briefing and to settle any remaining payments at our office, followed by dinner. Should your arrival be later in the day, arrangements will be made to complete payments and the briefing in Skardu.

Day 02: Flight to Skardu, Karakoram

Overview
• Altitude: 2,498 m
Participants will embark on a scenic flight from Islamabad to Skardu Airport, with the possibility of catching a glimpse of Nanga Parbat, weather permitting. Upon arrival in Skardu, the remainder of the day is yours to explore at your leisure.

Day 03: Free Day in Skardu

Overview
• Altitude: 2,498 m
After breakfast, participants can choose to hike to Kharpocho Fort, where stunning views of the Indus River and Skardu town await. There is also the option to visit Sadpara Lake, followed by free time for shopping in Skardu Bazaar. Throughout the day, our staff will handle any necessary government documentation, which may take up to two days. We have built-in contingency days at the end of the trek to accommodate any potential delays.

Day 04: Drive to Askole Village

Overview
• Altitude: 3,015 m
Participants will set off on a jeep safari to Daso, traveling through the picturesque Shigar Valley alongside the Braldu River until we reach Askole, the last village on our route. This journey will take approximately 6 to 8 hours, with participants possibly starting their trek before arriving in Askole, depending on road conditions.

Day 05: Trek from Askole to Jhola via Biafo Glacier Snout

Overview
• Altitude: 3,103 m
• Distance: 20 km
• Duration: 5-8 hours
After preparing the necessary supplies and equipment, porters will load up for the trek to Jhola. Participants will experience moraine walking as they cross the glacier snout, descending to a lovely lunch spot beside the Korofon River. The route will lead to the confluence of the Braldu and Domordo rivers, following a new trail upstream and across a bridge, before continuing along the riverbank to Jhola camp.

Day 06: Trek from Jhola to Paiju

Overview
• Altitude: 3,418 m
• Distance: 19.8 km
• Duration: 6-7 hours
Participants will trek along the Braldu gorge, enjoying breathtaking views of Trango Tower and Cathedral Peak. Given the potentially dry and hot conditions, precautions against sunburn are advisable. Depending on water levels, river crossings may require special shoes. The day concludes with a climb away from the river to camp at Paiju, the last campsite with trees for some time.

Day 07: Acclimatization Day at Paiju

Overview
• Altitude: 3,418 m
Participants will take the day to rest and acclimatize at Paiju Camp. During this time, porters will bake bread for the upcoming week on the glacier, and optional acclimatization walks to Paiju Peak base camp are available.

Day 08: Trek from Paiju to Khoburtse

Overview
• Altitude: 3,788 m
• Distance: 14.7 km
• Duration: 5-7 hours
As the trek becomes more challenging, participants will approach the snout of Baltoro Glacier. The route features continuous elevation changes on glacial moraine, offering stunning views of Trango Tower and Uli Biaho. Participants will traverse the glacier to Liligo, following a rocky trail along the Baltoro’s edge to reach Khoburtse camp.

Day 09: Cross Small Glaciers to Urdukus

Overview
• Altitude: 3,905 m
• Distance: 6.4 km
• Duration: 4-6 hours
After navigating two small glaciers, participants will camp at Urdukus, conveniently located near an army camp and set 100 meters above the glacier.

Day 10: Trek to Goro II

Overview
• Altitude: 4,285 m
• Distance: 11.9 km
• Duration: 6-8 hours
Participants will trek through the heart of the glacier, following the medial moraine. Stunning views of Masherbrum (7,821 m) will unfold along the way, with camp set at Goro II, where the Baltoro and Younghusband glaciers meet. Be prepared for a significant drop in temperatures as you take in breathtaking vistas.

Day 11: Trek to Concordia

Overview
• Altitude: 4,512 m
• Distance: 11.7 km
• Duration: 5-7 hours
Participants will reach Concordia, where towering snow-capped peaks come into view, culminating in the spectacular sight of K2, alongside Broad Peak, Mitre Peak, Gasherbrum, and Sia Kangri.

Day 12: Trek to Broad Peak Base Camp and K2 Base Camp

Overview
• Time: K2 BC (5,155 m), Gilkey (5,230 m), Broad Peak (4,844 m): 6-7 hours
This remarkable trek allows you to walk up the Godwin-Austen glacier to the Art Gilkey Memorial, commemorating those lost on K2. Departing early, you will cross glaciers along a faint trail towards K2, which will loom ever larger. After a lunch stop at Broad Peak Base Camp, the group will continue toward K2 Base Camp, where the landscape is adorned with boulders and ice. Overnight will be spent at K2 Base Camp. Should you feel unwell on this day and prefer not to stay at K2 Base Camp, we encourage you to consult your guide, as we prioritize the dreams and well-being of all trekkers.

Day 13: Return Trek to Concordia

Overview
• Time: 4-5 hours
Participants will retrace their steps back to Concordia, where they can rest and prepare for the next leg of the journey.

Day 14: Trek to Ali Camp

On this day, participants will take a less explored route, with detours to navigate around crevasses. Basic skills for crossing the Gondogoro La Pass will be taught upon reaching Ali Camp, named after the first local porter to successfully cross the pass.

Day 15: Trek to Khuispang over Gondogoro La

Participants will rise early, around 2 AM, to begin the ascent of Gondogoro La Pass. This challenging trek rewards adventurers with breathtaking views of four 8,000-meter peaks in the Baltoro region (K2, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum II). Care must be taken while descending, utilizing fixed ropes for safety, and the camp will be set at Khuispang.

Day 16: Trek to Saicho

Participants will descend towards Saicho, transitioning from rocky terrain to lush landscapes. A delightful lunch will be enjoyed along the way, with various trails leading to your destination. The day concludes with camp set up at Saicho, characterized by sandy areas and flowing glacier streams.

Day 17: Trek to Hushe

Overview
• Altitude: 2,498 m
• Distance: 11 km trek
• Duration: 5-7 hours trek
Participants will trek down for approximately 3-4 hours, witnessing the signs of habitation as they approach Hushe. After exploring the valley and interacting with the warm-hearted locals, the group will stay overnight in Hushe.

Day 18: Drive to Skardu

Overview
• Distance: 127 km Drive
After exploring the valley and mingling with the locals, the group will drive to Skardu Town, enjoying scenic views along the way. Participants can indulge in amenities, including hot showers and delicious meals.

Day 19: Flight to Islamabad

Participants will take a flight from Skardu to Islamabad, followed by a chance to relax at the hotel.
Note: Domestic flights may be subject to cancellation due to weather conditions. In the event of a cancellation, overnight travel to Chilas will be arranged, which will take approximately 8 to 10 hours by vehicle.

Day 20: Contingency Day for Flight Cancellations

This day has been set aside for any potential flight delays. Guests will depart early from Chilas to Islamabad, which may take up to ten hours. If the flight operates as scheduled, the day will be free for sightseeing in Islamabad.

Day 21: Departure to Home Country

Overview
• Meals Included: Breakfast
Our dedicated staff will assist guests with their airport transfers based on individual departure timings. Please be reminded that the checkout time for all partner hotels is set at 12 PM.

After navigating two small glaciers, participants will camp at Urdukus, conveniently located near an army camp and set 100 meters above the glacier.

Day 10: Trek to Goro II

Overview
• Altitude: 4,285 m
• Distance: 11.9 km
• Duration: 6-8 hours
Participants will trek through the heart of the glacier, following the medial moraine. Stunning views of Masherbrum (7,821 m) will unfold along the way, with camp set at Goro II, where the Baltoro and Younghusband glaciers meet. Be prepared for a significant drop in temperatures as you take in breathtaking vistas.

Day 11: Trek to Concordia

Overview
• Altitude: 4,512 m
• Distance: 11.7 km
• Duration: 5-7 hours
Participants will reach Concordia, where towering snow-capped peaks come into view, culminating in the spectacular sight of K2, alongside Broad Peak, Mitre Peak, Gasherbrum, and Sia Kangri.

Day 12: Trek to Broad Peak Base Camp and K2 Base Camp

Overview
• Time: K2 BC (5,155 m), Gilkey (5,230 m), Broad Peak (4,844 m): 6-7 hours
This remarkable trek allows you to walk up the Godwin-Austen glacier to the Art Gilkey Memorial, commemorating those lost on K2. Departing early, you will cross glaciers along a faint trail towards K2, which will loom ever larger. After a lunch stop at Broad Peak Base Camp, the group will continue toward K2 Base Camp, where the landscape is adorned with boulders and ice. Overnight will be spent at K2 Base Camp. Should you feel unwell on this day and prefer not to stay at K2 Base Camp, we encourage you to consult your guide, as we prioritize the dreams and well-being of all trekkers.

Day 13: Return Trek to Concordia

Overview
• Time: 4-5 hours
Participants will retrace their steps back to Concordia, where they can rest and prepare for the next leg of the journey.

Day 14: Trek to Ali Camp

On this day, participants will take a less explored route, with detours to navigate around crevasses. Basic skills for crossing the Gondogoro La Pass will be taught upon reaching Ali Camp, named after the first local porter to successfully cross the pass.

Day 15: Trek to Khuispang over Gondogoro La

Participants will rise early, around 2 AM, to begin the ascent of Gondogoro La Pass. This challenging trek rewards adventurers with breathtaking views of four 8,000-meter peaks in the Baltoro region (K2, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum II). Care must be taken while descending, utilizing fixed ropes for safety, and the camp will be set at Khuispang.

Day 16: Trek to Saicho

Participants will descend towards Saicho, transitioning from rocky terrain to lush landscapes. A delightful lunch will be enjoyed along the way, with various trails leading to your destination. The day concludes with camp set up at Saicho, characterized by sandy areas and flowing glacier streams.

Day 17: Trek to Hushe

Overview
• Altitude: 2,498 m
• Distance: 11 km trek
• Duration: 5-7 hours trek
Participants will trek down for approximately 3-4 hours, witnessing the signs of habitation as they approach Hushe. After exploring the valley and interacting with the warm-hearted locals, the group will stay overnight in Hushe.

Day 18: Drive to Skardu

Overview
• Distance: 127 km Drive
After exploring the valley and mingling with the locals, the group will drive to Skardu Town, enjoying scenic views along the way. Participants can indulge in amenities, including hot showers and delicious meals.

Day 19: Flight to Islamabad

Participants will take a flight from Skardu to Islamabad, followed by a chance to relax at the hotel.
Note: Domestic flights may be subject to cancellation due to weather conditions. In the event of a cancellation, overnight travel to Chilas will be arranged, which will take approximately 8 to 10 hours by vehicle.

Day 20: Contingency Day for Flight Cancellations

This day has been set aside for any potential flight delays. Guests will depart early from Chilas to Islamabad, which may take up to ten hours. If the flight operates as scheduled, the day will be free for sightseeing in Islamabad.

Day 21: Departure to Home Country

Overview
• Meals Included: Breakfast
Our dedicated staff will assist guests with their airport transfers based on individual departure timings. Please be reminded that the checkout time for all partner hotels is set at 12 PM.

Packing List

Embarking on the K2 & Gondogoro La Trek requires the right equipment to ensure safety, comfort, and success. We have categorized the required gear into three distinct lists to help you pack efficiently and be well-prepared for this demanding adventure.

Essential Gear

  • These mandatory items are crucial for your trek and should be included in your packing list:

    • First Aid Kit: Diamox (for altitude sickness), Dioralyte (rehydration salts), antiseptic cream, blister treatment, throat lozenges, adhesive plasters, Imodium (for diarrhea), painkillers.
    • Backpack (Daypack): 32–42 liters.
    • Insulation & Clothing:
      • Fleece jacket with hood or a warm sweater.
      • Warm gloves or mittens.
      • Thermal gloves.
      • Baselayer thermal shirts (two long-sleeve, two short-sleeve).
      • Baselayer thermal leggings.
      • Trekking trousers.
      • Waterproof jacket.
      • Waterproof over-trousers.
      • Shirts/T-shirts.
      • Walking socks (2–3 pairs).
      • Spare laces.
      • Underwear (regular and thermal).
    • Footwear:
      • High-quality hiking boots.
      • Sports sandals or old shoes (for river crossings).
    • Headgear & Accessories:
      • Warm hat.
      • Sun hat.
      • Sunglasses.
      • Headtorch with spare batteries.
    • Camping & Sleeping Gear:
      • Sleeping bag (-16°C comfort rating).
      • Sleeping mat (Thermarest or equivalent).
    • Hydration & Hygiene:
      • Water bottles (1 liter × 2).
      • Antibacterial hand wash.
      • Small towel.
      • Wash bag and toiletries.
    • Additional Essentials:
      • Trekking poles (highly recommended).
      • Down jacket (warm).
      • Mountaineering equipment (see List 2 below).

Mountaineering Equipment

  • For the Gondogoro La pass, additional technical gear is required:

    • Crampons.
    • Mountaineering boots (must be compatible with crampons, minimum Grade B2).
    • Ice axe.
    • Climbing harness.
    • Screwgate carabiners (x2).
    • Climbing helmet.
    • Prusik loops (x2) (4 meters of 6mm cord can be used to make two loops).
    • 120 cm sling.

Optional Items

While not mandatory, these items may add comfort and convenience to your trekking experience:

  • Buff or scarf.
  • Small padlock (for securing your bag).
  • Camera.
  • Insect repellent.
  • Multi-tool or pen knife (must be packed in checked luggage).
  • Basic repair kit (thread, needle, duct tape, etc.).
  • Sleeping bag liner.
  • Travel clothes for pre- and post-trek.
  • Bottle for personal hygiene (pee bottle).

FAQs

01

What are the best months for trekking in Pakistan?

+

 The best trekking season is from June to September, when temperatures are stable, and most passes are snow-free. For treks involving Gondogoro La Pass, July and August offer and for Snow Lake August is the safest conditions.

02

How physically demanding are these treks?

+

Each trek varies in difficulty:

  • K2 Base Camp Trek – Strenuous but non-technical, requiring good fitness.
  • Snow Lake Trek – Challenging due to glacier travel and isolation.
  • K2 Base Camp & Gondogoro La Circuit Trek – Demanding, with technical sections requiring crampons.
03

Do I need prior trekking experience?

+

Experience is not mandatory but recommended. You should be comfortable walking 6-8 hours per day on rocky and glacial terrain. Proper physical preparation is essential.

04

What permits do I need?

+
  • K2 Base Camp & Gondogoro La Trek require a special Mountaineering & Trekking Visa (not a regular tourist visa).
  • Snow Lake Trek requires a regular visa as this is not located in a restricted zone, which we arrange for you.
05

What happens in case of an emergency?

+
  • Our guides carry satellite phones for emergencies.
  • If altitude sickness occurs, you will be escorted to a lower altitude.
  • In severe cases, a helicopter rescue can be arranged (insurance required).
06

What fitness level and skills are required for K2 Treks?

+
  • K2 Base Camp Trek: Suitable for fit individuals with previous hiking experience. Trekkers walk 6-8 miles per day for 5-6 hours on rough terrain.

Gondogoro La Pass: Requires use of crampons and ropes due to snow, ice, and steeper climbs.

07

How far will we walk each day?

+
  • K2 Base Camp Trek: Expect to walk 8 to 14 km per day, taking 6-8 hours.
  • Gondogoro La Pass: The crossing day can take 8-12 hours, depending on snow conditions.
08

What’s the most challenging section of the trek?

+
  • K2 Base Camp Trek: The trek from Concordia to K2 Base Camp is challenging due to altitude and glacier terrain.
  • Gondogoro La Pass: The most difficult part is the steep ascent and descent over icy slopes.
09

What is the highest point reached?

+

Gondogoro La Pass at 5,585m.

10

How difficult is the Gondogoro La crossing?

+

 This is the most challenging section of the trek. The steep ascent and descent require fixed ropes, crampons, and an ice axe.

11

What happens if the pass is unsafe to cross?

+

 If conditions are dangerous, the group will return via the Baltoro Glacier.

12

What safety measures are in place?

+
  • Professional mountain guides manage rope sections.
  • Fixed safety lines are installed in technical sections.
  • Weather updates are constantly monitored.

Overview

About This Trip

Karachi, Pakistan’s bustling metropolis, is a city rich in history, culture, and coastal charm. This full-day tour takes you through the city’s most iconic landmarks, from the grand Mazar-e-Quaid to the artistic beauty of Mohatta Palace and the colonial-era elegance of Frere Hall. Stroll through the historic Empress Market and Saddar, where old meets new in a vibrant atmosphere. Enjoy a delicious local meal before exploring Dolmen Mall for an optional shopping stop. Finally, end the day at Port Grand, where the sea breeze, scenic views, and lively ambiance create the perfect closing to an unforgettable Karachi experience.

Why This Tour?

✅ Historical & Cultural Exploration – Visit Karachi’s most significant landmarks, from Mazar-e-Quaid to Mohatta Palace.
✅ Colonial Heritage Walk – Experience the charm of British-era architecture at Frere Hall and Saddar.
✅ Local Flavors – Savor Karachi’s famous cuisine at one of the city’s best restaurants.
✅ Optional Shopping Experience – Stop at Dolmen Mall for a mix of local and international brands.
✅ Scenic Waterfront Relaxation – Enjoy the stunning views and vibrant atmosphere at Port Grand.
✅ Hassle-Free Tour – Includes hotel pick-up and drop-off, ensuring a smooth and well-organized experience.

Itinerary

Your guide will pick you up from your hotel, and we’ll start exploring the vibrant and historic city of Karachi.

Mazar-e-Quaid (Quaid-e-Azam’s Mausoleum)

Visit the final resting place of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the founder of Pakistan. This iconic white marble mausoleum is a symbol of national pride and history.

Mohatta Palace

Explore the Mohatta Palace, a stunning heritage building that now serves as a museum showcasing art, history, and culture.

Empress Market & Saddar Heritage Walk

Take a walk through the Saddar area, home to beautiful colonial-era buildings and the bustling Empress Market, one of Karachi’s oldest and most famous markets.

Frere Hall

A beautiful British-era building surrounded by gardens, Frere Hall is a great place to experience Karachi’s architectural charm.

Lunch at a Local Restaurant

Enjoy Karachi’s famous cuisine at one of the city’s best restaurants

Dolmen Mall (Optional Shopping Stop)

If you’d like to shop, we can visit Dolmen Mall, Karachi’s top shopping destination, offering local and international brands.

Port Grand

End the day at Port Grand, a scenic waterfront entertainment and dining area where you can enjoy a relaxing walk, delicious street food, and a beautiful sunset view.

Drop-off at Hotel

After an exciting day exploring Karachi, your guide will drop you back at your hotel.

(Tour Starts and Ends in Karachi – If some other city additional Charges will apply)

Key Information

  • Destinations Covered: Mazar-e-Quaid, Mohatta Palace, Empress Market & Saddar Heritage Walk, Frere Hall, Dolmen Mall (optional), Port Grand.
  • Tour Duration: Full-day tour (8-10 hours).
  • Best Season: Year-round (Winter and Spring offer the best weather).
  • Difficulty Level: Easy – Suitable for all ages, with moderate walking.
  • Starting & Ending Point: Karachi (Hotel pickup & drop-off included).
  • Entry Requirements: No special permits required; foreign travelers should carry identification.
  • Meals: Lunch at a local restaurant.
  • Transport: Private vehicle with driver and English-speaking guide.
  • Additional Costs: Entry fees (if applicable), personal expenses, and optional shopping.
  • Customizations: Available upon request (special pickup from another city may incur additional charges).

FAQs

01

What is included in the Karachi Day Trip?

+

The trip includes hotel pick-up and drop-off, a guided tour of key landmarks, a private vehicle with a driver, and a visit to all listed attractions. Meals, entry fees (if applicable), and personal expenses are not included.

02

What is the duration of the tour?

+

The tour lasts approximately 8 to 10 hours, depending on traffic and time spent at each destination.

03

Is this tour suitable for all age groups?

+

Yes! The tour is designed for all ages with moderate walking involved.

04

What should I wear for the trip?

+

Karachi has a warm climate most of the year. Wear light, breathable clothing, comfortable walking shoes, and carry sunglasses and sunscreen. In winter, a light sweater may be needed.

05

Are meals included in the package?

+

Lunch at a local restaurant is included. However, personal snacks, beverages, and additional meals are not covered.

06

Is there an option for shopping during the trip?

+

Yes, there is an optional shopping stop at Dolmen Mall, where you can explore local and international brands.

07

Will there be a guide during the tour?

+

Yes, a professional English-speaking guide will accompany you throughout the tour.

08

Can I customize the itinerary?

+

Yes, customizations are possible. However, additional charges may apply for modifications or special pickups from another city.

09

Is the tour wheelchair/stroller accessible?

+

Most locations are wheelchair and stroller accessible, but some heritage sites may have stairs or uneven pathways. Let us know in advance so we can make necessary arrangements.

10

What happens in case of bad weather?

+

The tour operates in all weather conditions. However, in extreme situations, alternative arrangements may be suggested.

About This Trip

Kartarpur Sahib, one of the holiest sites in Sikhism, is a place of deep spiritual significance and unity. This full-day trip takes you on a journey to the revered Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, where Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism, spent the last years of his life. With a seamless travel experience, this tour allows you to immerse yourself in the peaceful and sacred atmosphere of Kartarpur, learn about Sikh heritage, and witness the architectural beauty of the Gurdwara. Whether you seek spiritual enlightenment, cultural exploration, or simply a serene retreat, this trip offers a profound and unforgettable experience.

Why This Trip?

✅ Sacred Experience – Visit one of the most important pilgrimage sites in Sikhism, where Guru Nanak Dev Ji spent his final years.
✅ Cultural & Historical Insight – Learn about Sikh heritage, Guru Nanak’s teachings, and the significance of Kartarpur.
✅ Architectural Marvel – Explore the stunning white marble Gurdwara, a symbol of peace and unity.
✅ Hassle-Free Travel – A guided tour with seamless immigration procedures ensures a smooth and comfortable journey.
✅ Serene Environment – Experience the tranquility of the Ravi River surroundings and meditate in the peaceful prayer halls.
✅ Optional Culinary Delight – Enjoy a traditional Punjabi meal for an authentic cultural experience.

Itinerary

Your guide will pick you up from your hotel, and we’ll begin our journey to Kartarpur Sahib, one of the most significant Sikh pilgrimage sites in the world.

Departure for Kartarpur Sahib

  • From Islamabad: Early morning departure for Kartarpur Sahib (Approx. 4.5 – 5 hrs drive, 380 km).
  • From Lahore: Early morning departure for Kartarpur Sahib (Approx. 2.5 hrs drive, 130 km).
  • Scenic drive along the M-11 Motorway passing through rural Punjab.

Arrival at Kartarpur Corridor

  • Arrive at the Kartarpur Corridor Terminal and complete immigration procedures.
  • Meet with the tour guide and begin the exploration of Gurdwara Darbar Sahib.

Explore Gurdwara Darbar Sahib

  • Visit the final resting place of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism.
  • Explore the beautifully restored white marble Gurdwara, one of the holiest sites in Sikhism.
  • Learn about Sikh history, the significance of Kartarpur, and Guru Nanak’s teachings.
  • Walk through the Langar Hall, where free meals are served to all visitors.
  • Spend time in the meditation area and prayer halls for a peaceful experience.
  • Capture breathtaking views of the Ravi River and the surrounding landscapes.

Lunch Break (Optional Stop)

  • Optional stop at a local restaurant near Kartarpur for a traditional Punjabi meal.

Return Journey

  • Complete immigration formalities at the Kartarpur Corridor Terminal.
  • Drive back to Lahore or Islamabad.
  • Drop-off at your location, marking the end of a spiritually enriching journey.

FAQs

01

Who can visit Kartarpur Sahib?

+

Kartarpur Sahib is open to Sikh pilgrims and visitors of all faiths. Both Pakistani and international travelers can visit, but foreign visitors must follow the necessary visa or permit requirements.

02

Do I need a visa to visit Kartarpur Sahib?

+
  • Pakistani Citizens: No visa is required; a valid CNIC is enough.
  • Indian Citizens: Can visit via the Kartarpur Corridor with an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA). No visa is required, but pre-registration is mandatory.
  • Other Foreign Nationals: May need a visa; check with local authorities before planning the trip.
03

What are the opening hours of Kartarpur Sahib?

+

The Gurdwara is usually open from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, but hours may vary based on immigration and border control policies.

04

Is there an entry fee for Kartarpur Sahib?

+

There is no entry fee for Pakistani visitors. However, foreign travelers (especially Indian pilgrims) may have to pay a service fee for using the Kartarpur Corridor.

05

What should I wear when visiting Kartarpur Sahib?

+

Visitors should wear modest clothing (no shorts, sleeveless tops, or revealing attire). Both men and women must cover their heads inside the Gurdwara (scarves or head coverings are usually available on-site).

06

Are meals available at the Gurdwara?

+

Yes, Langar (community kitchen) offers free meals to all visitors, regardless of religion or nationality. Visitors can also eat at nearby restaurants.

07

Can I take photographs inside the Gurdwara?

+

Yes, photography is allowed in most areas, but visitors should be respectful and avoid taking photos inside prayer halls.

08

How long does it take to complete the visit?

+

The visit usually takes 2-3 hours, but it may take longer if there are immigration procedures involved. The full trip from Lahore takes about 6-8 hours, while from Islamabad, it may take 10-12 hours round-trip.

09

Is transportation provided for the tour?

+

Yes, this tour includes private transport with a driver and guide for a hassle-free experience.

10

Can the trip be customized?

+

Yes! Special pickup and drop-off points, additional sightseeing stops, or meal preferences can be arranged upon request. Additional charges may apply.

Overview

About This Trip

Embark on an exciting day trip from Islamabad to Khewra Salt Mine, the second-largest salt mine in the world, known for its mesmerizing salt formations and centuries-old history. This tour takes you deep into the heart of the mine, where breathtaking salt carvings, glowing crystal structures, and underground wonders await. If time allows, we will also visit the Katas Raj Temples, an ancient Hindu temple complex with a sacred pond, adding a cultural and spiritual touch to your journey.

Why This Tour?

✅ Explore a Natural Wonder – Visit one of the world’s largest salt mines, featuring salt-carved landmarks and underground tunnels.
✅ Historical & Cultural Experience – Discover the mine’s connection to Alexander the Great and explore the rich Hindu heritage at Katas Raj Temples.
✅ Scenic Drive – Enjoy a comfortable journey through picturesque landscapes along the M-2 Motorway.
✅ Unique Attractions – Witness the famous salt mosque, Sheesh Mahal, and Minar-e-Pakistan carved from salt.
✅ Perfect Day Escape – A hassle-free, well-planned excursion from Islamabad, ideal for families, photographers, and adventure seekers.

Itinerary

Your guide will pick you up from your hotel in Islamabad, and we’ll begin our journey to Khewra Salt Mine, the world’s second-largest salt mine and one of Pakistan’s most fascinating natural wonders.

Departure from Islamabad

  • Early morning departure for Khewra Salt Mine (200 km – Approx. 3.5 hrs drive).
  • Scenic drive along the M-2 Motorway passing through picturesque landscapes.

Khewra Salt Mine Exploration

  • Arrive at Khewra Salt Mine and start an exciting guided tour inside the tunnels.
  • Learn about the history and discovery of the mine dating back to Alexander the Great’s era.
  • Witness stunning salt formations, stalactites, and stalagmites inside the mine.
  • Visit famous landmarks inside the mine, including:
    • The Badshahi Mosque made entirely of salt bricks.
    • The Sheesh Mahal (Palace of Mirrors) featuring glowing pink salt crystals.
    • The Miniature Minar-e-Pakistan & Great Wall of China carved from salt.
    • The Saltwater Ponds, known for their reflective beauty.
    • The Salt Therapy Chambers, believed to help with respiratory issues.
  • Experience the unique electric train ride inside the mine (optional).
  • Enjoy the breathtaking light illuminations inside the tunnels.

Lunch Break (Optional Stop)

  • Short break at a local restaurant near Khewra (as per client preference).

Katas Raj Temples

  • If time allows, visit the historic Katas Raj Temples, an ancient Hindu temple complex near Khewra.
  • Explore the stunning sacred pond, temple structures, and historical ruins.

Return to Islamabad

  • Drive back to Islamabad, concluding a memorable day exploring the Khewra Salt Mine.
  • Drop-off at your location.

Tour Details

  • Tour Starts & Ends in Islamabad (Additional charges apply for pickup from other cities).
  • Recommended Season: October to March for a comfortable experience.

Overview

About Expedition

The Khosar Gang Expedition is an ideal 6000m peak climb, offering a challenging yet achievable mountaineering experience in the Karakoram Range. Towering at 6,046m (19,837 ft), Khosar Gang is a lesser-known gem, providing climbers with stunning views of Skardu, Indus Valley, and the snow-capped peaks of the Karakoram. This 15-day adventure blends high-altitude trekking, technical climbing, and cultural immersion through Skardu and Sildi Valley, making it perfect for those looking to push their limits while experiencing Pakistan’s remote mountain beauty.

Why This Expedition?

    • Conquer a 6000m Peak: A moderate yet rewarding climb, ideal for climbers aiming to gain high-altitude experience and step into 6000m+ mountaineering.
    •  Breathtaking Scenery: Trek through Skardu, Sildi Valley, and glacier landscapes, experiencing the raw beauty of Pakistan’s northern mountain ranges.
    •  Technical Climbing Challenge: Includes snow, ice, and rocky terrain, allowing participants to develop mountaineering skills with fixed ropes and ascenders.
    •  Expert-Led Expedition: Guided by Summit Experts’ professional climbing leaders, ensuring safety, acclimatization, and proper logistics throughout the ascent.
    • Cultural & Local Experience: Connect with Balti traditions while passing through remote mountain villages, learning about local customs and way of life.

Itinerary

Day 01: Arrive at Islamabad International Airport

Altitude: 590 m 

Details: 

Welcome to Islamabad! Our team from Summit Experts Pakistan will be at the airport to greet  you, holding a name tag card for easy identification. Once you meet up with us, we will transfer  you to your hotel. Depending on your arrival time, you may have some spare time to visit a  nearby money exchange. Our billing department will also stop by to collect the remaining  payment. After dinner, it is off to bed, as we will be flying to Skardu the next day!

Day 02: Fly to Skardu, Karakoram

Altitude: 2,498 m 

Details: 

Today, we will take a scenic flight to Skardu International Airport. Once you arrive, settle into  your hotel and breathe in the fresh mountain air! Our guide will check your equipment, and after  lunch, you will have some free time to explore, acclimatize, or pick up a local SIM card for  communication.

Day 03: Spend Free Day in Skardu

Altitude: 2,598 m 

Details: 

Enjoy a leisurely day in Skardu! We will arrange a sightseeing tour, and if you need to purchase  any gear, we can visit the local market together.

Day 04: Drive to Sildi and Hike to Base Camp

Altitude: 3,800 m 

Details: 

Today marks the beginning of our adventure! We will embark on a 6-hour drive to Sildi Valley,  followed by a hike to establish our base camp. Get ready for a bumpy ride!

Day 05: Rest and Acclimatization Day at Base Camp

Altitude: 3,800 m 

Details: 

Take this day to relax and acclimatize at base camp. It’s a great opportunity to connect with  nature and prepare for the challenges ahead.

Day 06: Climb to Camp 1 for Overnight

Altitude: 4,800 m 

Details: 

Today we ascend to Camp 1, which will be a challenging climb taking approximately 6-8 hours,  depending on your physical fitness. It’s an important step in our journey!

Day 07: Climb to Camp 2 for Overnight

Altitude: 5,200 m 

Details: 

We will continue our ascent today, making our way to Camp 2. This climb is expected to take  about 5-6 hours and will require a mix of determination and stamina.

Day 08-10: Climbing Days for Summit Push

Altitude: 6,046 m 

Details: 

These days are dedicated to our summit push, contingent on favorable weather conditions. We  will rest at Camp 2 and keep our fingers crossed for a good weather window. With our  experienced guides, the success rate for this peak is nearly 90%, so stay optimistic!

Day 11: Return from Camp 2 to Base Camp

Altitude: 3,800 m 

Details: 

After our climbing days, we will descend back to base camp for a well-deserved overnight stay.  If you are interested in heading back to Skardu, please coordinate with your guide to arrange  transportation, as we will stick to the itinerary.

Day 12: Return to Skardu from Base Camp via Sildi

Altitude: 2,498 m 

Details: 

We will drive back to Skardu today, where you can relax at the hotel and reflect on your journey.

Day 13: Fly to Islamabad

Altitude: 590 m 

Details:Today, we will fly back to Islamabad. Enjoy your time at the hotel and take a moment to unwind  after your adventure.

Day 14: Contingency Day for Flight Cancellations

Details: 

If our flight is canceled, we will use this day for a scenic drive from Naran/Besham to Islamabad.  If you’re already in Islamabad, we’ll explore the city together.

Day 15: Fly to Home Country

Details: 

Most flights depart at midnight, so after some sightseeing, we will bid you a heartfelt farewell.  Our driver and guide will ensure you arrive at the airport three hours before your departure.

FAQs

01

What is included in the All-Inclusive Package, and what is not?

+

The All-Inclusive Package provides a comprehensive trekking and climbing experience, covering all logistics, accommodations, meals, permits, and guiding services from arrival to departure.

Included in the All-Inclusive Package:

  • Domestic flights (Checked baggage: 20kg, Hand carry: 7kg)
  • All road transfers (including airport transfers)
  • Hotel accommodation in Pakistan (twin sharing)
  • Trekking accommodation (twin-sharing dome tent)
  • All camping site and bridge fees
  • Trekking logistics (tents, non-personal equipment, tools)
  • All meals during the climb (breakfast, lunch, dinner)
  • Snacks, dry fruits, and tea/coffee during the trek
  • Free refills of boiled drinking water on the trek
  • Licensed professional guide (as per government requirements)
  • Mountain guide (for equipment orientation, rope fixing, summit guidance)
  • High-altitude group gear (ropes, ice screws, snow bars, EPI gas, tents, cooking pots)
  • All government fees and paperwork
  • Islamabad and Skardu city tours (including all entry fees)
  • Support staff (cook, assistants)
  • Personal luggage porter (14kg) & mountaineering equipment porter (13kg)
  • Storage service for baggage in Skardu
  • Basic first-aid kit
  • Satellite phone for emergencies
  • Trekking map & trip achievement certificate

Not Included in the All-Inclusive Package:

  • Personal travel insurance (recommended rescue partners: Global Rescue)
  • Visa for Pakistan (supporting documents provided)
  • International airfare
  • Personal trekking/mountain equipment (shoes, ice axe, crampons, harness, helmet, etc.)
  • Extra nights in Islamabad (USD 67 per night)
  • Additional trek baggage (USD 13 per kg)
  • Baggage storage in Islamabad (USD 28 per bag/piece)
  • Tips/gratuities for guides, porters, and staff
  • Personal expenses (minibar, bottled water, phone calls, laundry, souvenirs)
  • Early windup/return costs (if returning early due to personal reasons)
  • Costs due to force majeure (earthquake, landslides, floods, etc.)
02

What is included in the Climb-Only Package, and what is not?

+

The Climb-Only Package is designed for self-sufficient climbers who need essential trekking and climbing logistics but prefer to manage their accommodation, transport, and other personal expenses separately.

Included in the Climb-Only Package:

  • Trekking logistics (all tents, non-personal equipment, tools)
  • All meals during the climb (breakfast, lunch, dinner)
  • Snacks, dry fruits, tea/coffee during the trek
  • Free refills of boiled drinking water
  • Licensed professional guide
  • Mountain guide for equipment orientation, rope fixing, summit guidance
  • High-altitude group gear (ropes, ice screws, snow bars, EPI gas, twin-sharing tent, cooking pots)
  • All government fees and paperwork
  • Islamabad and Skardu city tours (including all entry fees)
  • Support staff (cook, assistants)
  • Personal luggage porter (14kg) & mountaineering equipment porter (13kg)
  • Storage service for baggage in Skardu
  • Basic first-aid kit
  • Satellite phone for emergencies
  • Trekking map & trip achievement certificate

Not Included in the Climb-Only Package:

  • Domestic flights
  • Road transfers (including airport transfers)
  • Hotel accommodation in Pakistan (Islamabad & Skardu)
  • Trekking accommodation (dome tents)
  • All camping site and bridge fees
  • Personal travel insurance
  • Visa for Pakistan
  • International airfare
  • Personal trekking/mountain equipment
  • Extra nights in Islamabad (USD 67 per night)
  • Additional trek baggage (USD 13 per kg)
  • Baggage storage in Islamabad (USD 28 per bag/piece)
  • Tips/gratuities for guides, porters, and staff
  • Personal expenses (minibar, bottled water, phone calls, laundry, souvenirs)
  • Early windup/return costs
  • Costs due to force majeure
03

What are the weather conditions like for each climb?

+

Weather conditions vary depending on the mountain and season. Typically, the best climbing window is between June and September, when conditions are more stable. However, strong winds, snowfall, and sub-zero temperatures are still common at high altitudes.

04

How do I train for high-altitude climbing?

+
  •  Climbers should prepare with a combination of cardio endurance, strength training, and altitude acclimatization. We recommend long hikes with a weighted pack, stair training, and high-altitude simulations if possible.
05

What kind of food will be provided at base camp and high camps?

+
  •  We provide a mix of Pakistani, Western, and high-energy expedition meals. Base camp meals include fresh vegetables, meats, pasta, rice, and soups, while high camps rely on freeze-dried and lightweight meals for easy preparation.
06

How much weight will I need to carry during the climb?

+
    • For Khosar Gang and Spantik, you will carry a light daypack (5-8kg) while porters transport heavier loads.
    For Broad Peak, climbers carry their own gear above base camp, typically 12-15kg including climbing equipment.
07

Can I hire a personal climbing guide or high-altitude porter?

+
  •  Yes, personal guides and porters are available at an additional cost. We highly recommend hiring a high-altitude porter for Broad Peak due to the extreme difficulty of carrying heavy loads above 7,000m.
08

What type of insurance do I need?

+
  •  Climbers must have comprehensive insurance covering high-altitude mountaineering, emergency rescue, and medical evacuation. A helicopter evacuation in the Karakoram can cost between $20,000 and $32,000 USD, so proper coverage is essential.
09

What happens if the weather prevents a summit attempt?

+

 If the weather prevents a summit bid, we will wait for a safer window or descend and return if necessary. Expedition dates include buffer days for flexibility, but we always prioritize safety over reaching the summit.

10

What is the group size for each expedition?

+
  • Khosar Gang: 4-10 climbers
  • Spantik Peak: 5-12 climbers
  • Broad Peak: 6-14 climbers Smaller groups allow for better logistics and individualized support.
11

How difficult is climbing Khosar Gang Peak?

+

Khosar Gang is an excellent introductory climb for those new to mountaineering. It involves basic ice axe, rope, and crampon use, but does not require advanced technical climbing skills.

12

What prior experience do I need?

+

While technical mountaineering experience is not required, you should have prior high-altitude trekking experience and be comfortable hiking on steep slopes and glacier terrain.

13

What equipment do I need for this climb?

+
  • Mandatory gear: B2 boots, crampons, ice axe, harness, and helmet.
  • Recommended gear: Trekking poles, high-altitude gloves, and a solar charger for electronics.
  • A complete packing list will be provided upon booking.
14

Do I need permits for Khosar Gang?

+

 No special permits are required, but we handle all necessary local permissions and logistics.

15

How long is the expedition?

+

 The standard itinerary is 9-12 days, including acclimatization and summit attempts.
